quickSummary: K₂Cr₂O₇ is synthesized from Chromite ore (FeCr₂O₄) via Na₂CrO₄ (yellow) and Na₂Cr₂O₇ (orange). Chromate (CrO₄²⁻, yellow) and Dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻, orange) interconvert via pH (acid yields orange; base yields yellow; OS remains +6). In acid, Cr₂O₇²⁻ has n-factor = 6 (E° = +1.33 V), oxidizing I⁻ to I₂, Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺, H₂S to S, and SO₃²⁻ to SO₄²⁻.
summary: Master potassium dichromate synthesis, pH-dependent chromate-dichromate equilibria, structures, and acidic redox stoichiometries.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5. Potassium Dichromate Industrial Synthesis
conceptBreakdown.title: 5. Potassium Dichromate Industrial Synthesis

summaryBox.title: K₂Cr₂O₇ Synthesis & Primary Standard
summaryBox.takeaway: FeCr₂O₄ + Na₂CO₃ + O₂ ──► Na₂CrO₄ (yellow) ──► Na₂Cr₂O₇ (orange) ──► K₂Cr₂O₇ crystals. K₂Cr₂O₇ is non-deliquescent and used as primary analytical standard.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
POTASSIUM DICHROMATE INDUSTRIAL SYNTHESIS
                      
   1. Chromite Ore Roasting: $4\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4 + 8\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 7\text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{1100^\circ\text{C}} \mathbf{8\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 \text{ (Yellow)}} + 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 8\text{CO}_2$
   2. Acidification:         $2\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 \text{ (Orange)}} + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
   3. Potassium Exchange:    $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 2\text{KCl} \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 \downarrow \text{ (Orange Crystals)}} + 2\text{NaCl}$
conceptBreakdown.content: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is crystallized because it is much less soluble in water and non-deliquescent compared to $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, making it an ideal primary analytical volumetric standard.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Chromate-Dichromate pH Equilibrium & Structures
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Chromate-Dichromate pH Equilibrium & Structures
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CHROMATE-DICHROMATE pH EQUILIBRIUM

2CrO₄²⁻ (Yellow) + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ (Orange) + H₂O

• In Acidic Medium (pH < 7): Orange Dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻) dominates.
• In Basic Medium (pH > 7): Yellow Chromate (CrO₄²⁻) dominates.
• Oxidation state of Cr is +6 in BOTH ions (Condensation, NOT redox!).

Structures:
• Chromate Ion (CrO₄²⁻): Tetrahedral (sp³), Cr = +6 (d⁰)
• Dichromate Ion (Cr₂O₇²⁻): Two corner-sharing tetrahedra with Cr-O-Cr bridge angle = 126°
conceptBreakdown.content:
Chromate ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$, yellow) and Dichromate ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$, orange) exist in dynamic equilibrium controlled by solution $\text{pH}$:
$$\mathbf{2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} \text{ (Yellow)} + 2\text{H}^+ \underset{\text{Base (OH}^-)}{\overset{\text{Acid (H}^+)}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \text{ (Orange)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Oxidizing Action of K₂Cr₂O₇ in Acidic Medium
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Oxidizing Action of K₂Cr₂O₇ in Acidic Medium
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
OXIDIZING ACTION OF K₂Cr₂O₇ (n = 6)

Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ ──► 2Cr³⁺ (Green) + 7H₂O  (E° = +1.33 V)

Key Oxidations:
1. Iodide to Iodine:       Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6I⁻ ──► 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O + 3I₂
2. Ferrous to Ferric:      Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ ──► 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O + 6Fe³⁺
3. H₂S to Sulfur:          Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 8H⁺ + 3H₂S ──► 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O + 3S↓ (Turbidity)
4. Sulfite to Sulfate:     Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 8H⁺ + 3SO₃²⁻ ──► 2Cr³⁺ + 4H₂O + 3SO₄²⁻
conceptBreakdown.content:
In acidic solution, Dichromate acts as a powerful oxidant ($n\text{-factor} = 6$):
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} (+6) + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \longrightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} (+3) \text{ (Green)} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \quad (E^\circ = +1.33\text{ V})$$

quickRevision: K₂Cr₂O₇ is synthesized from FeCr₂O₄ (chromite ore).
Yellow CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O (Cr remains +6).
Cr-O-Cr bridging angle in Cr₂O₇²⁻ is 126°.
In acid, Cr₂O₇²⁻ n-factor = 6 (reduces to green Cr³⁺).
Cr₂O₇²⁻ oxidizes I⁻ ──► I₂, Fe²⁺ ──► Fe³⁺, H₂S ──► S↓, SO₃²⁻ ──► SO₄²⁻.
